corpus_purpose: Phase G regression/falsification corpus. Ten systems, run end to end through the pipeline. A system whose actual pipeline output does not match expected_findings/expected_evidence_levels is a methodology or software defect, not a false positive to be prompted away.

systems.name: Read-only internal knowledge agent
systems.description: Answers employee questions from an internal wiki. No write access anywhere.
systems.authority_map_summary: agent -> reads -> data_source(wiki). No other edges.

expected_findings.title: Wiki content poisoning could mislead downstream answers

systems.expected_reviewer_intervention: Minimal, confirm no write edges were missed in extraction. Good baseline case, should NOT generate a critical finding, if it does, the deterministic rules are over-firing.

systems.name: Customer-support agent with CRM access
systems.description: Reads and writes customer records, drafts replies for human send.
systems.authority_map_summary: agent -> reads/writes -> data_source(CRM); agent -> calls -> tool(draft_email, requires_human_approval=true).

expected_findings.title: CRM write scope broader than support-reply use case requires

systems.expected_reviewer_intervention: Verify the human-approval flag on email sending is real (see SYN-10 for the failure mode where it is present but meaningless).

systems.name: Agent capable of sending emails autonomously
systems.description: Sends emails without a human-approval step, unlike SYN-02.

expected_findings.title: Irreversible external communication with no human checkpoint

systems.expected_reviewer_intervention: Confirm severity should not be 'critical', this is high not critical absent financial/data-exfiltration compounding, tests whether the deterministic rule in 05-ASSESSMENT-ENGINE.md over- or under-calibrates.

systems.name: Agent capable of financial transactions
systems.description: Can initiate payments via a payment API, no approval step documented.
systems.authority_map_summary: agent -> calls -> api(payment_api, requires_human_approval=false, action_reversibility=irreversible, data_classification=restricted).

expected_findings.title: Agent can execute irreversible financial transactions without human authorization

systems.expected_reviewer_intervention: This is the primary vertical-slice test case (09-VERTICAL-SLICE.md). The critical finding must NOT be diluted by any other finding on this same system, and must remain visible at E1 (documentation review only) until a reviewer actually tests the approval gate.

systems.name: Agent with excessive database privileges
systems.description: Documentation says 'read customer table', actual connection string documented elsewhere in the intake material grants full schema access.
systems.authority_map_summary: agent -> reads -> data_source(customer_table) [as documented]; contradicts a separately uploaded config extract showing broader grants.

expected_findings.title: Documented access scope contradicts actual granted privileges

systems.expected_reviewer_intervention: This is an adversarial case (Phase 20): the LLM extraction step must surface the contradiction in 'unresolved_questions' (architecture-extraction.schema.json) rather than silently picking one source over the other.

systems.name: Agent using an external MCP/tool provider
systems.description: Delegates a sub-task to a third-party MCP server outside the client's infrastructure.

expected_findings.title: Third-party MCP server is an unaudited supply-chain dependency with system access

systems.expected_reviewer_intervention: Check whether the client can even produce evidence about the third party's own controls, likely caps this finding at E1 indefinitely unless the client escalates to the vendor, a realistic and worth-reporting limitation.

systems.name: Multi-agent orchestration system
systems.description: A coordinator agent delegates to three sub-agents, each with different tool access.
systems.authority_map_summary: agent(coordinator) -> delegates_to -> agent(sub_1, sub_2, sub_3), each with distinct edges to tools/data.

expected_findings.title: No documented containment boundary if one sub-agent is compromised
Cascading failure path: sub_1's output feeds sub_2's tool call without validation

systems.expected_reviewer_intervention: Tests whether the Authority Map correctly represents delegation chains as distinct edges rather than collapsing the coordinator and sub-agents into one node.

systems.name: Agent with persistent memory
systems.description: Retains conversation history and user preferences across sessions, feeds future responses.

expected_findings.title: No documented mechanism to detect or purge poisoned memory entries

systems.expected_reviewer_intervention: Baseline memory-poisoning case, should map cleanly to ASI06 without needing a compound finding.

systems.name: Agent processing sensitive customer information
systems.description: Reads PII and payment-adjacent data to answer support queries, no explicit data-loss-prevention control documented.
systems.authority_map_summary: agent -> reads -> data_source(customer_pii, data_classification=restricted); agent -> calls -> tool(external_search, trust_boundary=external).

expected_findings.title: Restricted data reachable by a tool call that can cross an external trust boundary, no outbound DLP control documented

systems.expected_reviewer_intervention: This is the composition case from the decision brief's core diagnostic question, no single edge looks dangerous alone, the read and the external call together are the risk. Tests whether the Framework Mapper (02-ARCHITECTURE.md) actually reasons over paths, not just individual edges.

systems.name: Agent with inadequate human approval boundaries
systems.description: requires_human_approval is set to true in the documentation, but the intake material shows the 'approval' is an auto-acknowledged notification with no actual blocking step.
systems.authority_map_summary: agent -> calls -> tool(critical_action, requires_human_approval=true) [as documented, contradicted by workflow description elsewhere in the same intake].

expected_findings.title: Documented human-approval control does not function as a real blocking checkpoint

systems.expected_reviewer_intervention: The sharpest adversarial case in the corpus: this is exactly 'human approval is technically present but meaningless' from Phase 20. If the pipeline reports this system as having adequate human oversight because requires_human_approval=true was taken at face value, the methodology has failed this test.

corpus_level_pass_criteria: No synthetic system's critical finding is diluted or hidden by any scoring or averaging mechanism.
SYN-05 and SYN-10 specifically must surface their contradictions rather than silently resolving them in the LLM extraction step.
SYN-09 must be caught by path-level reasoning, not edge-level reasoning alone.
No finding across any of the ten systems is created at evidence_level above E1 during automated diagnostics, only a Reviewer or test_harness action may create E2 or above.
